lines.text: Many learners say: I bought a gift to my mother.
Better: I bought a gift for my mother.
The first! I made a cake for her.

data.wrong: I bought a gift to my mother.
data.right: I bought a gift for my mother.

options: I made a cake for her.
I made a cake to her.

native.tip: Para dizer quem recebe algo comprado ou feito, use “for”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I bought a gift to my mother.” O certo é “I bought a gift for my mother.” Em português “para” serve para tudo, mas em inglês comprar algo para alguém pede “for”. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “I made a cake for her.” Agora diga em voz alta uma frase sua com esse ponto e treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: To say who gets something you bought or made, use “for”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I bought a gift to my mother.” The right way is “I bought a gift for my mother.” In Portuguese “para” works for everything, but in English buying something for someone takes “for”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
